style: Hand-drawn 2D cartoon illustration for a YouTube history explainer. Simple stick-figure people with large round plain white heads, black dot eyes, expressive eyebrows, small simple mouths, messy dark hair, thin black stick arms and legs, teal striped hide tunics with a tooth necklace; thick clean black ink outlines, flat bright colors with soft painterly shading, richly detailed painted cartoon backgrounds (caves, savanna, firelight, starry skies). Funny, gentle, not gory. 16:9 widescreen. Absolutely no text, letters, captions or watermark in the image.

shots.p: Wide night shot of a savanna camp under a huge starry sky: a dozen stick-figure people asleep around a glowing hearth beside small domed grass huts, each wearing a small dark watch-like band on the wrist; acacia silhouettes and a big moon.
shots.line: Scientists once watched a group of hunter-gatherers sleep for twenty nights.

shots.p: Close-up over a sleeping camp at night: every single person fast asleep with tiny sleep bubbles, while a giant round sundial-style stone clock floats in the starry sky with only a thin glowing sliver of its face lit up.
shots.line: In all that time, everyone was asleep at the same moment for just eighteen minutes.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) sitting up wide-eyed in his grass bed at night, eyebrows shooting up in astonishment, campfire embers glowing beside him, cave mouth and stars behind.
shots.line: Eighteen minutes. In twenty nights.

shots.p: Hero shot: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) yawning hugely, stretching his stick arms at the entrance of a firelit cave at dusk, a soft grass bed inside, orange sky and mountains behind, cosy and funny.
shots.line: So how did ancient humans actually sleep?

shots.p: Three-panel comic split: left, Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) poking a pile of grass; middle, a lion's glowing eyes peering from dark bushes at a sleeping camp; right, Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) lying awake staring at the stars.
shots.line: Where did they lie down? Who kept the lions away? And did they really sleep like we do?

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) leaning toward the viewer with a mischievous raised eyebrow, holding a flaming torch under his chin like telling a spooky campfire story, dark cave behind.
shots.line: The answer is weirder than you think.

shots.p: Full-body portrait of Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) standing in a sunny savanna at late afternoon, droopy eyelids, slumped shoulders, dragging a wooden spear behind him, a funny yawn.
shots.line: Meet Moss. He's a Stone Age human, and he is very, very tired.

shots.p: Over-the-shoulder shot from behind Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) as he trudges toward a rocky hill with a cave mouth glowing orange at sunset, his shadow long on the grass.
shots.line: Tonight, we're going to follow him to bed.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) peering up curiously into a tall leafy tree where a friendly cartoon chimpanzee peeks down at him; warm evening forest light.
shots.line: Let's start with our cousins.

shots.p: A cartoon chimpanzee high in a tree canopy at sunset bending leafy branches into a round bowl-shaped nest, a few leaves fluttering, golden light through the forest.
shots.line: Every evening, a wild chimpanzee climbs a tree and builds itself a fresh bed of bent branches and leaves.

shots.p: Close-up of the chimpanzee lying comfortably in its finished leafy tree nest, arms behind its head, looking smug and relaxed, pink dusk sky behind.
shots.line: It takes just a few minutes.

shots.p: Wide shot of a small group of early humans, led by Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace), walking out of a forest edge onto open savanna, waving goodbye to a chimpanzee in a tree.
shots.line: At some point, our ancestors came down from the trees for good.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) lying on bare dry grass on the open savanna at night, looking nervous, eyes darting sideways, dark bushes around him under a big moon.
shots.line: And sleeping on the ground comes with a problem.

shots.p: Low-angle close-up of tall grass at night with several pairs of glowing yellow eyes peering out, cartoonish rather than scary.
shots.line: Things with teeth.

shots.p: Wide moonlit savanna: a lion silhouette on a rock, a leopard lounging on an acacia branch and a hyena slinking through the grass, all cartoony, a starry violet sky.
shots.line: Lions, leopards, hyenas. The night belonged to them.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) crouching and carefully blowing on a tiny glowing ember in a nest of dry grass, his face lit orange, darkness around him.
shots.line: So humans did something no other animal does.

shots.p: A cosy campfire blazing beside a sleeping Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) curled up on the ground, warm orange light forming a safe bubble in the dark, glowing animal eyes keeping their distance at the edge.
shots.line: They brought fire to bed.

shots.p: Inside a huge deep cave with a wide arched entrance, a modern archaeologist with a brush and headlamp kneeling by a dig trench showing a thin dark grey ash layer and small blackened bone fragments.
shots.line: In Wonderwerk Cave, in South Africa, scientists found ash and burned bone about a million years old.

shots.p: Cutaway view of the same cave long ago: a small group of early humans sitting around a small fire deep inside, warm glow on the rock walls.
shots.line: That's one of the earliest signs of fire being used inside a cave.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) warming his hands at a fire inside a cave mouth while, outside in the dark, a cartoon hyena sits down grumpily and refuses to come closer.
shots.line: Fire meant warmth. It meant light. And it may have helped keep hungry animals at a distance.

shots.p: Wide shot of a starry night sky above a cave entrance, a group of people gathered around a fire, the moon rising, a feeling of calm.
shots.line: Scientists think it also gave people something new: evenings.

shots.p: Around a campfire, Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) waves his arms telling a dramatic story, shadow of a mammoth cast on the cave wall, children and adults laughing and sharing roasted roots.
shots.line: Time to sit together, share food, and tell stories, after the sun went down.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) trying to lie down on lumpy rocks next to the fire, wincing, one eyebrow up, a pointy stone poking his back.
shots.line: But a fire doesn't make a bed.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) looking amazed as a soft golden glow falls on a fluffy pile of grass in the back of a cave, like a treasure discovered.
shots.line: And this is where the evidence gets surprisingly cosy.

shots.p: Wide shot of a cave high in a rocky cliff above green hills, with a modern archaeologist's ladder and string grid at the entrance, morning light.
shots.line: In Border Cave, in South Africa, archaeologists found the remains of beds made around two hundred thousand years ago.

shots.p: Close-up of a dig trench wall showing thin pale fossil-grass layers sandwiched between grey ash, with a small trowel and a magnifying glass resting beside it.
shots.line: They are the oldest known grass beds ever found.

shots.p: Inside a cave, Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) carrying a big bundle of broad green grass and spreading it at the back of the cave beside a glowing hearth.
shots.line: They were made of bundles of broad-leafed grass, laid near the back of the cave, close to the fire.

shots.p: Cosy wide shot of Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) lying on his grass bed at the back of the cave, fire glowing nearby, the dark cave entrance far away in the background.
shots.line: The warmest, safest spot in the house.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) tapping the side of his head with one finger, eyes gleaming, a little lightbulb-shaped glowing ember floating above his head.
shots.line: But here's the clever part.

shots.p: Cutaway cross-section of the bed like a layer cake: green grass on top, a thick layer of soft grey ash below, cave floor at the bottom, Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) peeking at it from the side.
shots.line: Underneath the grass, there was a layer of ash.

shots.p: Close-up of the cave floor where a line of tiny cartoon ants and beetles marches up to a grey ash patch and stops, looking confused.
shots.line: Scientists think the ash was a bug barrier.

shots.p: Extreme close-up of a funny cartoon beetle wading through grey powder up to its knees, coughing a little puff of dust, looking annoyed.
shots.line: Crawling insects struggle to move through fine powder, and ash can clog up the tiny holes they breathe through.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) tucking sprigs of a grey-green aromatic bush into his bed while a cloud of mosquitoes turns around and flies away in a huff.
shots.line: On one bed, they even found burned bits of camphor bush, a plant that people in South Africa still use to keep insects away.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) holding his nose and lifting a corner of a flattened brown old grass bed, with a few cartoon bugs waving up at him.
shots.line: And when a bed got old and buggy?

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) standing back as the old grass bed burns in a small controlled fire inside the cave; inset scene beside it shows him spreading fresh green grass over the cooled ash.
shots.line: They seem to have burned it. Then they laid fresh grass on top of the ashes.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) proudly holding a leafy branch like a broom in front of a fresh tidy bed, sparkles around it, hands on hips.
shots.line: Stone Age spring cleaning.

shots.p: Wide shot of a big rock shelter under an overhanging cliff above a green river valley, lush forest, a group of people living under the overhang.
shots.line: Fast forward to about seventy-seven thousand years ago, at another South African site called Sibudu.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) and a friend wading at a sparkling riverbank pulling up armfuls of tall green rushes and sedges, a heron watching.
shots.line: Here, people stacked up mattresses of sedges and rushes, picked from a nearby river.

shots.p: Daytime inside the rock shelter: a wide flat mattress of layered rushes where Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) sits knapping a stone tool while a child naps beside him.
shots.line: Some covered up to three square metres. Big enough to sleep on, sit on, and work on during the day.

shots.p: Close-up of Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace)'s hands laying glossy dark green leaves from a leafy riverside tree on top of the rush mattress.
shots.line: And on top, they added leaves from a tree called the river wild-quince.

shots.p: A cartoon mosquito approaching the leafy bed, then recoiling dramatically with its legs in the air and its nose pinched, little stink lines rising from the leaves.
shots.line: Those leaves contain natural chemicals that kill insects, and they'd be good at repelling mosquitoes.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) lying back luxuriously on his leafy bed by the fire, hands behind his head, totally relaxed, at night in the rock shelter.
shots.line: So these people had soft beds, bug spray, and a fire.

shots.p: Over-the-shoulder shot from behind a sleeping Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace): beyond the firelight, the dark bush with a pair of glowing eyes, everyone in camp asleep.
shots.line: But they still had one big problem. Who stays awake to watch for danger?

shots.p: The giant floating stone clock from earlier hovering over a sleeping savanna camp at night, its thin glowing sliver shining.
shots.line: To find out, let's go back to those eighteen minutes.

shots.p: Wide daytime landscape of dry Tanzanian savanna with baobab trees, rocky hills and a modern-day hunter-gatherer camp of domed grass huts, people in simple modern clothing, respectful and friendly.
shots.line: The study was done with the Hadza, hunter-gatherers who live in Tanzania today.

shots.p: Night scene of a camp: some people sleeping outside on animal skins by a small hearth, others inside dome-shaped huts woven from grass and branches, stars overhead.
shots.line: They sleep in groups of twenty to thirty, outside by the hearth or in huts of grass and branches.

shots.p: Close-up of a hand with a small dark wristband sensor resting on an animal skin beside an ember, a gentle moonlit glow.
shots.line: Thirty-three adults wore little watch-like sensors on their wrists for twenty days.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) holding out a spear to his sleeping friends as if offering the night-watch job, and every one of them is snoring and ignoring him.
shots.line: Here's the funny part. Nobody was given the job of night guard.

shots.p: An empty little lookout rock beside a sleeping camp, with nobody standing on it, the moon shining, crickets in the grass.
shots.line: The Hadza generally don't post lookouts at all.

shots.p: A row of five sleepers lying side by side at night, each with a different little moon or sun symbol floating above them showing different sleep times.
shots.line: Instead, people's body clocks were naturally different.

shots.p: Comic triptych: a young caveman awake late beside a real owl on a branch; an older cavewoman stretching at dawn beside a chirping bird; a third caveman blinking awake mid-night, scratching his head.
shots.line: Some were night owls. Some were early birds. And some just woke up a lot.

shots.p: A grey-haired cartoon grandpa caveman with a walking stick yawning and climbing into bed while the sky is still pink with sunset, younger people still chatting by the fire.
shots.line: Older adults, in their fifties and sixties, tended to go to bed earlier and wake up earlier.

shots.p: Top-down view of a sleeping camp around a hearth at night, with one or two figures softly glowing as they lie awake and listen, the rest dimmed and asleep.
shots.line: So at almost any moment of the night, someone was awake, or only lightly asleep.

shots.p: A wise cartoon grandma caveman sitting upright by the embers at night, one eye open, alert, with a protective soft glow around the sleeping group behind her.
shots.line: Scientists call this the sentinel idea.

shots.p: Funny scene: the grey-haired grandpa caveman wide awake at 4 a.m. by the fire, glaring into the dark bushes where a cartoon lion slinks away embarrassed.
shots.line: Your grumpy, early-rising grandpa might have been the best security system the Stone Age had.

shots.p: Daytime scene of a friendly modern Hadza family by their grass hut in modern simple clothing, one holding a bow, warm and respectful.
shots.line: Of course, the Hadza aren't time travellers. They're modern people with their own lives.

shots.p: Split image: left, a modern bedroom lit by a glowing phone and lamp at midnight; right, Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) asleep in darkness lit only by embers and stars.
shots.line: But studying them gives scientists clues about how humans slept before electric lights.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) smashing a giant fragile clay pot with a stone club, the pieces flying, a look of cheeky delight.
shots.line: And those clues bust a few of our favourite myths.

shots.p: A big painted map-style landscape with three vignettes and no labels: a Tanzanian savanna with baobabs, the red sand Kalahari desert with scrub, and a green Bolivian rainforest with a river, connected by a dotted path.
shots.line: In another study, scientists tracked the sleep of three groups: the Hadza, the San in the Kalahari, and the Tsimane in Bolivia.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) imagining himself in a dream bubble sleeping like a log, snoring for ages under a pile of furs, cobwebs forming on him.
shots.line: You might expect them to sleep ten hours a night.

shots.p: A large cartoon hourglass beside a sleeping figure, its sand only partly run through, a rooster on a rock at dawn.
shots.line: Nope. They slept between about five point seven and seven point one hours.

shots.p: Side-by-side: an office worker in pyjamas yawning at an alarm clock in a city apartment, and Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) yawning at dawn in his cave, both with the same sleepy expression.
shots.line: That's about the same as many people in modern cities, or even a bit less.

shots.p: Twilight savanna turning to deep blue night, a group still sitting up chatting around a small fire, nobody lying down yet.
shots.line: And they didn't go to bed when it got dark.

shots.p: Wide shot of the night sky with the moon high, stars bright, the camp finally lying down by dying embers.
shots.line: On average, they fell asleep more than three hours after sunset.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) sitting by the fire with a puzzled face, finger on chin, looking up at the stars.
shots.line: So what told them it was bedtime?

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) shivering a little as a soft blue chilly breeze swirls around him at night, pulling a hide blanket up to his chin.
shots.line: Scientists think the big clue was temperature.

shots.p: Pre-dawn scene, sky pale blue-grey with frosty dew on the grass, Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) sitting up awake, breath misting, the sun not yet over the horizon.
shots.line: They slept as the night cooled, and they usually woke up around the coldest part, just before sunrise.

shots.p: A modern person lying awake in bed at night staring at the ceiling with dark eye bags, a glowing phone on the nightstand.
shots.line: And here's the one that might make you jealous.

shots.p: A happy Tsimane-style villager asleep in a hammock under a thatched roof by a rainforest river, peaceful, fireflies around.
shots.line: The San and the Tsimane don't even have a word for insomnia.

shots.p: Wide shot of a large group of people all sleeping peacefully under the stars, and just one person sitting up with a grumpy face, comically outnumbered.
shots.line: Only a few people in every hundred said they regularly had trouble sleeping.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) holding up two fingers with a skeptical squint, a candle-lit medieval cottage appearing in a thought bubble above him.
shots.line: Wait. Didn't people in the past sleep in two halves?

shots.p: A cosy medieval European cottage at night, snow outside the window, a family asleep in a big wooden bed under a patchwork quilt.
shots.line: You might have heard about first sleep and second sleep.

shots.p: A historian at a desk piled high with old scrolls, leather books and wax-sealed letters, reading by lamplight with a magnifying glass; no readable writing visible.
shots.line: Historian Roger Ekirch found hundreds of mentions of it in old European diaries, letters and court records.

shots.p: Inside the medieval cottage at midnight: a family awake in bed by candlelight, one person stoking the fire, another quietly praying, a cat watching.
shots.line: People went to bed, woke up for an hour or so in the middle of the night, then went back to sleep.

shots.p: A snowy northern European village under a very long dark winter night, tiny glowing windows, a crescent moon.
shots.line: But that's from the last few hundred years, mostly in Europe, where winter nights are long.

shots.p: Warm savanna night: a hunter-gatherer group sleeping soundly in one long peaceful stretch beside a small hearth, a shooting star overhead.
shots.line: The hunter-gatherers in these studies mostly slept in one stretch.

shots.p: Funny courtroom made of stone slabs in a cave: a jury of sleepy cavemen and a chimpanzee shrugging, Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) as the judge with a bone gavel.
shots.line: So for the Stone Age, the jury is still out.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) leaning in close to the camera with wide eyes in a dark cave, a single torch flickering, dramatic but playful.
shots.line: And then there's the strangest idea of all.

shots.p: A snowy mountainside in winter with a dark cave entrance, inside a small group of early humans curled up together under furs in a deep sleep, icicles at the entrance.
shots.line: In 2020, two scientists suggested that early humans in a Spanish cave, about four hundred thousand years ago, might have survived harsh winters by hibernating.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) curled up asleep snuggled against a big friendly cartoon brown bear inside a snowy cave, both snoring with little sleep bubbles.
shots.line: Like bears.

shots.p: A scientist in a clean lab looking at a clean cartoon bone fragment through a magnifying glass, a sleeping bear poster-style painting on the wall.
shots.line: They pointed to odd marks on the bones that look a bit like those in hibernating animals.

shots.p: The cartoon bear wide awake and grumpy in the cave, while Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) shivers and sneezes, clearly terrible at hibernating, wrapped in furs.
shots.line: But many experts aren't convinced. Those marks could have other causes, and big animals like us are bad at true hibernation.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) tossing a small clay tablet with a bear drawing into a woven 'maybe' basket full of odd curiosities, shrugging with a grin.
shots.line: So file that one under fun, but probably not.

shots.p: Wide establishing shot at dusk: a cliffside cave glowing with firelight above a river valley, stars appearing, Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) climbing up to it.
shots.line: So, here's what a night might have looked like for Moss.

shots.p: Close-up of a crackling campfire inside a cave, sparks drifting upward, warm orange and gold light on the rock.
shots.line: A fire crackling at the back of the cave.

shots.p: Cosy detailed close-up of Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace)'s bed: thick green grass and glossy leaves spread over grey ash, a camphor sprig tucked at the edge.
shots.line: A soft bed of grass on a layer of ash, with bug-repelling leaves on top.

shots.p: Warm group shot: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) with family and friends lying side by side under hide blankets, whispering and giggling, firelight on their faces.
shots.line: Friends and family lying close together, chatting long after sunset.

shots.p: Time-lapse style double scene: the group asleep under a cold starry sky, then Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) stretching at the cave mouth as the sky turns pink before sunrise.
shots.line: Sleep as the air turns cool. Up before the sun.

shots.p: Close-up of the grey-haired grandpa caveman lying on his side with one eye open in the firelight, ear perked, everyone else asleep behind him.
shots.line: And somewhere in the group, there's always someone half awake. Listening.

shots.p: The giant floating stone clock over the sleeping camp one last time, its thin glowing sliver shining in a starry sky.
shots.line: Remember those eighteen minutes?

shots.p: Wide aerial view of many campfires dotted across a dark savanna and cave-filled hills at night, each with a tiny figure sitting up awake beside sleeping groups.
shots.line: If the Hadza are any guide, our ancestors' camps were almost never all asleep at once.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) rolling over to sleep as his grandpa sits up to take the watch, a gentle handoff in the firelight, both smiling.
shots.line: We took turns without even trying.

shots.p: A modern kid in pyjamas sitting bolt upright in bed in a dark bedroom at 3 a.m., eyes wide, a curtain fluttering.
shots.line: So the next time a tiny noise wakes you at three in the morning, don't be annoyed.

shots.p: The same modern kid in bed, with a friendly ghostly Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) sitting beside them holding a tiny torch, both giving a thumbs up.
shots.line: You're just working your ancient night shift.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) waving goodbye from his cosy grass bed by the fire at the back of a cave, pulling up his hide blanket, starry cave mouth behind.
shots.line: Follow for more of how ancient humans really lived.
